sources: Tom Barrack, US Special Envoy to Syria and Iraq, speaking to Al Jazeera's Diplomatic Editor James Bays in Doha
fault_line: A serving US envoy admits US regime-change attempts have always been a mistake — so should the Iran war end now?

sections.what_happened: Barrack, asked whether the US-Israeli war on Iran was a mistake: 'I don't know whether it's a mistake or not,' acknowledging it has had 'unintended consequences' and calling the resulting situation 'horrible'. He said every US attempt to change a person/regime in the Middle East 'seems to have been a mistake' (23 regime changes, 'none had produced the intended results'); the initial objective was preventing an imminent nuclear threat, not regime change; Iran's political future must be decided by Iranians; the administration does not want the war to continue; a modified 'Islamabad understanding' could underpin renewed talks (ceasefire, reopening maritime routes, easing economic pressure).
sections.what_verified: Al Jazeera liveblog + AA wire with full verbatim quotes + Al Jazeera YouTube clip (VZ_pNPBjMhU) + restoflworldreport relay. Separate from his covered 'pointless' Yemen-intervention comment (same forum, different remarks).
sections.what_disputed: Barrack is one envoy, not a policy decision-maker; his 'mistake' framing on Iran is hedged ('I don't know'). No indication of an actual policy shift — CENTCOM carrier posture and blockade unchanged.
sections.why_matters: 'I don't know if it was a mistake' — the war's own envoy won't defend it. Run the quotes straight; the US admitting unintended consequences while the blockade grinds on is the story.
